thesis: The Tabernacle at Pendrell Vale taxes every creature each upkeep, turning a land into a sweeping economic rule that rewards decks built with few creatures and abundant mana denial.

canonicalIdentity.currentOracleText: All creatures have "At the beginning of your upkeep, destroy this creature unless you pay {1}."
canonicalIdentity.identityNotes: Legends #307 released June 1, 1994; original artist Nicola Leonard, IDs pinned to accepted card identity. Contemporary Oracle wording is not misrepresented as original 1994 text; original and later wording should be distinguished where possible.

originalContext.setEnvironment: Legends, June 1994, introduced The Tabernacle at Pendrell Vale. Its land slot produces no mana and grants an upkeep trigger to every creature.
originalContext.designPurpose: Rule-text analysis: a symmetric creature-maintenance obligation is made asymmetric when one deck has few creatures and the other has limited mana. No undocumented designer-intent claim.
originalContext.initialReception: No newly invented 1994 contemporary reviews. The dated 2015 Lands victory and player primer are evidence of a later competitive development.

loreContext.summary: Nicola Leonard's original land artwork supplies the visual identity; no particular canonical story or named inhabitant is asserted.

competitiveTimeline.significance: Nonmana legendary land gives all creatures beginning-of-controller-upkeep payment-or-destruction triggers.

Registered one Tabernacle, four Crop Rotation, four Wasteland, four Rishadan Port, three Maze of Ith and Loam/Stage-Depths engines; contemporaneous finals recap mentions Tabernacle's role in game one. Opening story is fictional, not a replay of that game.
Pilot-authored analysis documents the strategic land engine after the Grand Prix, distinguished from actual tournament game transcripts.

playbook.role: A nonmana land creates per-creature upkeep maintenance bills on both sides; a creature-light mana-denial deck can exploit those bills.
playbook.deckRequirements: Provide actual mana sources and separate win conditions; use land tutoring and engine effects to offset a nonmana utility slot; maintain few creatures or plan to pay their upkeep obligations.
playbook.copyCount: Jarvis Yu's published 2015 winning Lands deck had one Tabernacle; do not generalize to every Lands list.
playbook.mulligans: Hands that count Tabernacle as a mana-producing land risk being unable to cast Crop Rotation, Loam or other spells.
playbook.sequencing: Each creature controller controls and pays for their own beginning-of-upkeep triggers, after untap. Existing triggers persist if Tabernacle leaves the battlefield; playing Tabernacle after upkeep does not produce retroactive triggers.
playbook.sideboarding: The correct plan depends on creatures, noncreature engines and mana availability, not merely the presence of many opposing cards.
playbook.commonMistakes: Describing Tabernacle as a tapped activated ability, a sacrifice effect, a global sweeper, or a tax paid by Tabernacle's controller.

counterplay.directAnswers: Answer the land when legal, or keep enough available mana to pay for the creature count; play noncreature win conditions when useful.
counterplay.engineDisruption: Destroy or disrupt Wasteland/Port/Loam utility engines that constrain payment ability; fight the board state rather than only the legendary land.
counterplay.timingWindows: Triggers arise at the beginning of each creature controller's upkeep after untap; newly created creatures after the upkeep window do not owe the tax until a later upkeep. Removing Tabernacle after triggers exist does not automatically remove them.
counterplay.racing: Maintain fewer, more effective creatures or use noncombat victory conditions to minimize the number of upkeep obligations.
counterplay.sideboarding: Choose specific mana, land or noncreature answers appropriate to the format.

claims.summary: Legends #307, June 1994; originally illustrated by Nicola Leonard, a legendary land with no mana-production ability.

Tabernacle grants upkeep-triggered destroy-unless-pay-{1} text to each creature; controller of each creature controls its trigger and decides to pay as it resolves. Unpaid creatures are destroyed, not sacrificed; Tabernacle does not activate or tap.
Jarvis Yu won Grand Prix Seattle-Tacoma 2015 with one Tabernacle in Legacy Lands and the recorded Crop Rotation, Port, Wasteland and Maze supporting card pool.
A contemporary recap reports Tabernacle mattered in the first final game, but no transcript supports the precise constructed opening scene.

Opponent with Delver, Young Pyromancer, two tokens and two usable mana sources is a hypothetical 2015 Legacy matchup; four upkeep abilities and two payment choices are consistent with current rules, not actual Yu/Calcano gameplay.
